title: Site changes badge: one WP-Cron upgrade run (two plugins + one theme, three log rows within a second) counts as ONE on another seat's badge, a cron content edit counts nothing, and the tab's "N new" says the badge's number while every row of the run is lit
steps: Common setup (tests/regression/README.md § Common setup): ORIGIN (= O), PG, WEB, api, pq. Seats: A = owner (its cookie pulls the CMS log), C = another seat on the site (viewer or editor). Case variables: KEY = site key and LABEL = container prefix of a WordPress site (scv2: KEY=scv2wp.scv2.tracy.test, LABEL=scv2wp). Browser: chrome-watch on 127.0.0.1:9222; every page opens in its own browser context with only that seat's tracy_sess cookie (CDP Target.createBrowserContext).

Check the web build: docker exec $WEB grep -c 'softwareUnitOf' /opt/tracy-web/src/sites/activity-source.js must print >= 1; otherwise stop with BLOCKED note web-older-than-this-feature. Check WP-CLI: docker exec $LABEL-web-1 wp --allow-root --path=/var/www/html core version prints a version; otherwise BLOCKED note no-wp-cli.

The hook ignores WP-CLI on purpose (WP_CLI is a Tracy request to it), so cron rows come from wp-cron.php: write a mu-plugin that registers two cron hooks. docker exec $LABEL-web-1 mkdir -p /var/www/html/wp-content/mu-plugins, then docker exec -i $LABEL-web-1 tee /var/www/html/wp-content/mu-plugins/reg062.php with this PHP: `<?php add_action('tracy_reg062_upgrade', function () { do_action('upgrader_process_complete', null, ['action' => 'update', 'type' => 'plugin', 'plugins' => ['akismet/akismet.php', 'hello.php']]); do_action('upgrader_process_complete', null, ['action' => 'update', 'type' => 'theme', 'themes' => ['twentytwentyfive']]); }); add_action('tracy_reg062_content', function ($post_id) { wp_update_post(['ID' => (int) $post_id, 'post_title' => 'Hello world! (cron ' . time() . ')']); });` (the same WordPress action a real auto-update fires, with the same arguments). RUNCRON = docker exec $LABEL-web-1 wp --allow-root --path=/var/www/html eval 'echo wp_remote_retrieve_response_code(wp_remote_get("http://localhost/wp-cron.php?doing_wp_cron", ["timeout"=>90, "headers"=>["Host"=>parse_url(site_url(), PHP_URL_HOST)]]));' (must print 200). PULL = wait 6.5 s, then api a POST /api/sites/$KEY/cms-log/pull with body {} → its `pulled`.
Baseline for C: U0 = api c GET /api/sites/$KEY/activity/unseen → record U0.count and U0.since (the first ask writes the watermark at now).

One cron upgrade run: docker exec $LABEL-web-1 wp --allow-root --path=/var/www/html cron event schedule tracy_reg062_upgrade now; RUNCRON; wait 2 s; LOG = docker exec $LABEL-web-1 wp --allow-root --path=/var/www/html eval 'global $wpdb; foreach ($wpdb->get_results("select id, user_id, resource_type, resource_id, op, context from {$wpdb->prefix}tracy_admin_log order by id desc limit 3", ARRAY_A) as $r) echo implode(" | ", $r), "\n";' → record LOG. P1 = PULL → record. ROWS1 = pq "select op, resource_type, producer->>'context', occurred_at from site_cms_change where site_key='$KEY' and resource_type in ('plugin','theme') and producer->>'context'='cron' order by id desc limit 3" → record. U1 = api c GET /api/sites/$KEY/activity/unseen → record U1.count.

One cron content edit: POST = docker exec $LABEL-web-1 wp --allow-root --path=/var/www/html post list --post_type=post --post_status=publish --field=ID --posts_per_page=1 (empty → BLOCKED note no-published-post); docker exec $LABEL-web-1 wp --allow-root --path=/var/www/html cron event schedule tracy_reg062_content now --post_id=$POST (a 'Numeric keys' warning is fine); RUNCRON; P2 = PULL → record; ROW2 = pq "select op, resource_type, producer->>'context' from site_cms_change where site_key='$KEY' order by id desc limit 1" → record. U2 = api c GET /api/sites/$KEY/activity/unseen → record U2.count.

The V2 answer for C: V = api c GET /api/sites/$KEY/activity?version=2&filter=all&limit=6 → record V.unseenCount, V.seenBefore, and for each of the first 5 items {kind, origin.source, unit, unseen, description.params.type}.

The UI, seat C in a fresh context: open $O/$KEY/, wait for the .tv-start-card containing 'Site changes', wait 4 s; record CARD = its .tv-start-card-count text and title. Press the card; wait for [data-site-changes-v2] .tv-activity-event (up to 90 s), wait 3 s; record TAB = {rows, unread: count of .tv-activity-event[data-unread], divider: [data-new-divider] text, lit: the .tv-activity-desc-text of each [data-unread] row}. Then U3 = api c GET /api/sites/$KEY/activity/unseen → record U3.count. Leave the page open.
Clean up: docker exec $LABEL-web-1 rm /var/www/html/wp-content/mu-plugins/reg062.php (the cron events ran once and are gone; the post title keeps its stamp — a test site).
expect: LOG shows three rows with user_id 0, context 'cron': plugin akismet/akismet.php, plugin hello.php, theme twentytwentyfive, all op 'update'; P1 === 3; ROWS1 is those three rows with producer context 'cron' and occurred_at within two seconds of each other.
U1.count === U0.count + 1 — three software rows of one cron run are ONE thing (an island of one unit `wordpress-tracy-log:auto`).
P2 === 1; ROW2 is op 'update', resource_type 'post', context 'cron'; U2.count === U1.count — a cron content edit is on the list, never on the badge.

V.unseenCount === U2.count; the three software items have origin.source 'automatic', unit 'wordpress-tracy-log:auto' and unseen true; the post item has origin.source 'automatic', unit null and unseen false.

CARD.text === String(U2.count) (or '9+' past 9) and CARD.title names U2.count changes; TAB.divider matches new RegExp('^' + U2.count + ' new since you last looked') while TAB.unread >= 3 and TAB.lit includes the three software rows (akismet, hello.php, twentytwentyfive) — the badge's number on the divider, every row of the run lit; U3.count === 0 after the tab drew the list.
No step changed anything outside the test site; no page or context was closed.

selectors.rule: activity-source.js: BADGE_SOURCES (+deployment), softwareUnitOf / SOFTWARE_RESOURCE_TYPES / SOFTWARE_OPS, the `unit` column of V2_SOURCES_SQL, badgeRowSql; activity-store.js countUnseenV2 (islands of one unit at gaps < 2 s of occurred_at)
selectors.hook: wordpress tracy-access.php `upgrader_process_complete` → rows with context 'cron' when DOING_CRON; WP_CLI requests are ignored by design

evidence: tasks/evidence/site-changes-badge-count/reg-063/ (measured 04/10/2026 on the private stand `badge`: three cron rows pulled at 13:45:50 → C's count 0 → 1; a cron post edit → still 1; V2 unseenCount 1 with the three software rows unseen and the post row not; card 1, divider '1 new since you last looked', three rows lit). Dev data behind the rule: 28 no-user WordPress rows on 13 site-days, all plugin/theme/core installs and updates, against one site's 24,220-row catalogue sync.
fence: The badge counts the site's software changing whoever did it (a cron, a self-update, a Tracy deploy) and never cron content; software rows of one CMS log and one account within two seconds of the CMS clock are one thing, cut over every row of the unit so a run straddling the watermark counts once; content rows never group.
